data.title: Data Destruction
data.summary: The sample deletes or corrupts files at the filesystem level — individually or in bulk — as its primary impact, distinct from a full disk wipe and from ransomware's reversible encryption.
data.description:
This sits between the two more severe techniques: narrower than a disk wipe (specific
files or directories, not the whole volume) and, unlike ransomware, offering no recovery
path at all once complete — there is no key because nothing was encrypted, only destroyed.
Some variants target backup and shadow-copy locations specifically, as a precursor to or
substitute for a separate ransomware stage.
data.recommendation:
* Identify the specific scope targeted (file types, directories, backup locations) to establish what is actually unrecoverable versus merely inaccessible.
* Restore from offline backups not reachable by the sample's scope; prioritise recovering backup infrastructure first if it was itself a target.
* Treat backup- or shadow-copy-targeted destruction as a strong signal that a further-reaching attack (ransomware, wiper) was planned or already underway.
data.short_recommendation: Establish the destruction's exact scope, and check whether backup or shadow-copy locations were specifically targeted.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Recursively deleted files matching a target extension list and additionally targeted Volume Shadow Copy storage.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Deleted matching files directly via the filesystem API with no prior encryption or staging.
